solution:
"""
URL: https://leetcode.com/problems/design-a-stack-with-increment-operation/description/?envType=problem-list-v2&envId=vn57k9wr

1381. Design a Stack With Increment Operation

Design a stack that supports increment operations on its elements.

Implement the CustomStack class:

- CustomStack(int maxSize) Initializes the object with maxSize which is the maximum number of elements in the stack.
- void push(int x) Adds x to the top of the stack if the stack has not reached the maxSize.
- int pop() Pops and returns the top of the stack or -1 if the stack is empty.
- void inc(int k, int val) Increments the bottom k elements of the stack by val. If there are less than k elements in the stack, increment all the elements in the stack.

Example 1:

Input
["CustomStack","push","push","pop","push","push","push","increment","increment","pop","pop","pop","pop"]
[[3],[1],[2],[],[2],[3],[4],[5,100],[2,100],[],[],[],[]]
Output
[null,null,null,2,null,null,null,null,null,103,202,201,-1]
Explanation
CustomStack stk = new CustomStack(3); // Stack is Empty []
stk.push(1);                          // stack becomes [1]
stk.push(2);                          // stack becomes [1, 2]
stk.pop();                            // return 2 --> Return top of the stack 2, stack becomes [1]
stk.push(2);                          // stack becomes [1, 2]
stk.push(3);                          // stack becomes [1, 2, 3]
stk.push(4);                          // stack still [1, 2, 3], Do not add another elements as size is 4
stk.increment(5, 100);                // stack becomes [101, 102, 103]
stk.increment(2, 100);                // stack becomes [201, 202, 103]
stk.pop();                            // return 103 --> Return top of the stack 103, stack becomes [201, 202]
stk.pop();                            // return 202 --> Return top of the stack 202, stack becomes [201]
stk.pop();                            // return 201 --> Return top of the stack 201, stack becomes []
stk.pop();                            // return -1 --> Stack is empty return -1.

Constraints:

    1 <= maxSize, x, k <= 1000
    0 <= val <= 100
    At most 1000 calls will be made to each method of increment, push and pop each separately.
"""


class CustomStack:

    def __init__(self, maxSize: int):
        self.maxSize = maxSize
        self.stack = []
        self.inc_arr = [0] * maxSize

    def push(self, x: int) -> None:
        if len(self.stack) < self.maxSize:
            self.stack.append(x)

    def pop(self) -> int:
        if not self.stack:
            return -1
        i = len(self.stack) - 1
        inc_val = self.inc_arr[i]
        if i > 0:
            self.inc_arr[i - 1] += inc_val
        self.inc_arr[i] = 0
        return self.stack.pop() + inc_val

    def increment(self, k: int, val: int) -> None:
        limit = min(k, len(self.stack))
        if limit > 0:
            self.inc_arr[limit - 1] += val


sol = CustomStack(3)
sol.push(1)
sol.push(2)
print(sol.pop())  # 2
sol.push(2)
sol.push(3)
sol.push(4)
sol.increment(5, 100)
sol.increment(2, 100)
print(sol.pop())  # 103
print(sol.pop())  # 202
print(sol.pop())  # 201
print(sol.pop())  # -1

assert sol.pop() == -1

# Recreate the scenario for asserts to match example exactly
stk = CustomStack(3)
stk.push(1)
stk.push(2)
assert stk.pop() == 2
stk.push(2)
stk.push(3)
stk.push(4)
stk.increment(5, 100)
stk.increment(2, 100)
assert stk.pop() == 103
assert stk.pop() == 202
assert stk.pop() == 201
assert stk.pop() == -1

assert CustomStack(1).pop() == -1
